questions.question: Which language should the frontend use?

options.label: TypeScript
options.description: Typed JavaScript for a maintainable frontend.

options.label: JavaScript
options.description: Standard JavaScript with a lighter setup.

questions.rationale: A new frontend benefits from type safety, and no existing language was found.

questions.question: Which frontend framework or approach should the application use?

options.label: Nuxt 4
options.description: Full-stack Vue and TypeScript application with SSR and server routes.

options.label: Next.js
options.description: React with routing and optional server-rendering capabilities.

options.label: Vue with Vite
options.description: A component-based frontend with a concise template syntax.

options.label: Plain HTML, CSS, and JavaScript
options.description: A minimal static application without a framework.

questions.rationale: The supplied OKSBI specification requires Nuxt 4 with TypeScript, SSR, and server routes.

questions.question: What should the MUSIC PACKAGE application do? Describe the main screens, actions, and music-related workflow.
questions.answer: Production-grade music distribution, publishing administration, rights management, royalty reporting, payouts, smart links, Content ID workflows, support, copyright/takedown workflows, and separate admin operations. Build incrementally, starting with architecture, Nuxt configuration, Tailwind via Vite, three-mode color mode, PostgreSQL/Prisma, secure authentication, onboarding, and the normalized creator-rights-finance domain model. Keep distribution and publishing separate, use provider abstractions and mocks where external agreements are required, and protect private media and identity documents.

questions.question: Which data stores does the application need?

options.label: No datastore required
options.description: The application does not need persistent data, file storage, queues, or caching.

options.label: PostgreSQL
options.description: Relational application data and structured records.

options.label: Blob Storage
options.description: Audio, images, uploads, documents, or other media files.

options.label: Redis
options.description: Caching, sessions, or low-latency transient data.

questions.rationale: The supplied specification requires normalized PostgreSQL records, private media/document storage, and transient session/rate-limit infrastructure.

questions.question: Do users need to sign in to access application features?

options.label: Yes
options.description: Users have accounts and sign in to access application features.

options.label: No
options.description: The application is public or does not require user accounts.

questions.rationale: The specification requires server-managed opaque sessions, email verification, MFA, RBAC, CSRF protection, rate limiting, audit trails, and step-up authentication.
